approach: If the steel rod stays 4 cm longer than the copper rod at every temperature, both rods must expand equally for the same rise, fixing the length ratio.

steps.text: Write the change in length of each rod for the same temperature rise.
steps.equation: ΔL_steel = L_steel α_steel ΔT, ΔL_copper = L_copper α_copper ΔT

steps.text: The 4 cm gap stays fixed at every temperature only if both rods expand by the same amount.
steps.why_this_step: If the two expansions differed, the gap would change as the temperature changed, contradicting the question.

common_mistakes.text: Inverting the relation and writing L_copper/L_steel instead of L_steel/L_copper gives 11/17.
Mistaking the 4 cm gap as part of the ratio and writing the copper coefficient over 4 gives 17/4.
